nodes.name: Freedman method preparation
nodes.procedure: WO3, H2O was prepared by the Freedman method (26). WO3, 2H2O was prepared according to the Freedman (26) or Furusawa (27) methods.
nodes.source_text: Monoclinic WO3 and WO3, H2O are commercially available (Merck). The latter was also prepared for verification by the Freedman method (26). WO3, 2H2O was prepared according to the Freedman (26) or Furusawa (27) methods.

nodes.name: Furusawa method preparation
nodes.procedure: WO3, 2H2O was prepared according to the Furusawa method (27).
nodes.source_text: WO3, 2H2O was prepared according to the Freedman (26) or Furusawa (27) methods.

nodes.name: Literature preparation h-WO3
nodes.procedure: The preparations of h-WO3 have been described previously (3).
nodes.source_text: The preparations of h-WO3 and WO3, 1/3H2O have been described previously (3, 9).

nodes.name: Literature preparation WO3·1/3H2O
nodes.procedure: The preparations of WO3, 1/3H2O have been described previously (9).
nodes.source_text: The preparations of h-WO3 and WO3, 1/3H2O have been described previously (3, 9).

nodes.characterization_summary: m-WO3 Raman spectrum shows characteristic Ag and Bg modes with strong lines at 807, 715 cm⁻¹ (stretching), 273 cm⁻¹ (deformation), and lattice modes below 200 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the strong intensity of the Ag and Bg modes in Raman gives rise to rather well defined lines whereas broad adsorptions are observed in the infrared

nodes.characterization_summary: m-WO3 IR spectrum shows broad absorptions in stretching region (870, 815, 755, 665 cm⁻¹), deformation at 280 cm⁻¹, with effects from particle size and host medium.
nodes.evidence_snippet: small differences occur in the profile of the intense infrared band between 600 and 950 cm⁻¹ (10-12, 14, 16, 18, 19). As shown in Fig. 2 they may come from different sampling conditions.

nodes.characterization_summary: h-WO3 Raman spectrum (<100 mW laser) shows strong lines at 817, 253, 108 cm⁻¹, medium at 690, 162 cm⁻¹, clearly differentiated from m-WO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the actual Raman spectrum of h-WO3 presents strong lines at 817, 253, and 108 cm⁻¹ and medium lines at 690 and 162 cm⁻¹ which are clearly differentiated

nodes.characterization_summary: h-WO3 IR spectrum shows broad absorptions 1000-600 cm⁻¹ and 400-200 cm⁻¹, narrow 440 cm⁻¹ band specific to hexagonal W-O-W deformation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The infrared spectrum of h-WO3 present broad absorptions at 1000-600 and 400-200 cm⁻¹ and a much narrower band at 440 cm⁻¹ . The latter could well be specific of a deformation of the W-O-W bridge

nodes.characterization_summary: WO3·H2O IR shows ν(OH) 3390(3430), (3340), 3170(3220) cm⁻¹ splitting into three at 77K, δ(OH) 1620 cm⁻¹, ν(W=O) 948 cm⁻¹, ν(W-OH2) 370 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The former splits into three components at 77K . The low-frequency shoulder at ∼3220 cm⁻¹ can be assigned to the overtone 2δ(OH) of the δ(OH) mode at 1620 cm⁻¹

nodes.characterization_summary: WO3·H2O shows ν(W=O) at 948 cm⁻¹, broad O-W-O stretching at 645 cm⁻¹, ν(W-OH2) at 377 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It is easy to assign the 948-cm⁻¹ band present in the infrared and Raman spectra to the stretching mode of the terminal W=O bond.

nodes.characterization_summary: WO3·H2O INS at 348K confirms ν(W-OH2) ∼370 cm⁻¹ peak, shows quasielastic scattering from water reorientation (τ∼7×10⁻¹² s, EISF=0.85 at Q=2Å⁻¹).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The width of the Lorentzian σ (HWHH) fitted independently for each angle was found nearly constant at 0.18±0.02 meV , corresponding to a correlation time τ=2/σ of ∼7×10⁻¹² sec.

nodes.characterization_summary: WO3·2H2O IR shows three ν(W=O) 1007(1009), 945(945), 918(918) cm⁻¹, ν(OH) 3530(3550), 3370(3360), 3160(3120) cm⁻¹ from three H-bond families.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of three infrared absorptions at 1007, 945, and 918 cm⁻¹ and of one intense Raman line at 960 cm⁻¹ for WO3,2H2O (Fig. 6, Table I) can thus be explained

nodes.characterization_summary: WO3·2H2O shows intense ν(W=O) Raman line at 960 cm⁻¹ and ν(W-OH2) at 380 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a well defined Raman line is observed which could be the counterpart of the intense ν(W=O) vibration at 960 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: WO3·⅓H2O IR after degassing at 175°C shows structural ν(OH) 3550 cm⁻¹, δ(OH) 1609 cm⁻¹, ν(W=O) 950-1000 cm⁻¹; adsorbed H2O/OH bands 3220, 1410 cm⁻¹ disappear.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the bands at 1410 and 3220 cm⁻¹ are due to adsorbed species. The former cannot be assigned to water deformation... All the W=O surface groups may not have reacted as indicated by a band at 1000 cm⁻¹ which remains even after degassing.

nodes.characterization_summary: WO3·⅓H2O shows ν(W=O) at 945-948 cm⁻¹, bridging O at 805, 680 cm⁻¹, possible ν(W-OH2) at ~325 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the intrinsic structural properties of WO3,1/3H2O are reflected by the presence of a band at about 950 cm⁻¹ in the infrared and Raman spectra.
